extracted.intended_audience: students, educators, coaches, and general readers seeking an overview of mathematics competitions worldwide
extracted.subtask_description: A global, encyclopedic listing of mathematics competitions at international, regional, national, and collegiate levels, with brief notes on scope, eligibility, format, and organizers. Useful for finding competitions by grade level, geographic scope, or subject focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test format / question type
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests may require multiple choice or numeric answers, or a detailed written solution or proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page include multiple choice/numeric-answer formats and detailed written proofs; specialized contests emphasize particular formats (e.g., Integration Bee focuses on integral calculus problems, Mathematical Modeling contests require extended modeling solutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic scope / level
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitions are organized at different geographic scopes (international, multinational regional, national, college/university).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly groups contests into 'International mathematics competitions', 'Multinational regional mathematics competitions', and 'National mathematics olympiads' and lists examples like the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) and the William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: grade/age/student level
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitions specify eligible participant age or grade ranges (e.g., 'for all grade levels K-12', 'undergraduate students', 'grades 4–12').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'World Mathematics Invitational — for all grade levels K-12'; IMC — 'international competition for undergraduate students'; many national lists indicate grade bands and school levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team vs individual format
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitions are designated as team contests or individual contests (e.g., 'team contest for high school students', 'team contest for undergraduates', 'teams of girls representing different regions').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'China Girls Mathematical Olympiad — held annually for teams of girls representing different regions'; 'Mathematical Contest in Modeling (MCM) — team contest for undergraduates'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official languages of the papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Some competitions specify official languages for the contest materials (e.g., English and Chinese).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'World Mathematics Invitational — Taiwanese based ... with English and Chinese as the official languages of the papers.' Others note language orientation (e.g., mainly French-speaking countries) while allowing broader participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation restrictions: open vs invite-only / public-school-only
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitions indicate whether participation is open to all, limited to public-school students, or invite-only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Olimpíada Brasileira de Matemática (OBM) — national competition open to all students'; 'Olimpíada Brasileira de Matemática das Escolas Públicas (OBMEP) — open to public-school students'; 'Australian Mathematics Olympiad - Invite-only competition for top performing students'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / selection role
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contests serve as selection events for higher-level teams or further competitions (e.g., selection of national IMO teams).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Australian Mathematics Olympiad ... used to select the individuals who will sit the team selection test for the opportunity to represent Australia at the International Mathematical Olympiad'; 'Philippine Math Olympiad, the selection event ... for the Philippine IMO team.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject focus / specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain competitions target particular branches or skills in mathematics (e.g., integral calculus, modeling, mental calculation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Integration Bee — competition in integral calculus'; 'Mathematical Contest in Modeling (MCM) — modeling'; 'Mental Calculation World Cup — contest for the best mental calculators.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency / scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitions note their recurrence or timing (e.g., held annually, since 1959).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) — the oldest international Olympiad, occurring annually since 1959.' Many other contests are described as annual events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition structure / rounds and levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitions may be organized in multiple rounds or internal levels (e.g., two rounds, levels named Explorer/Discovery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Vietnam ... Consists of 2 rounds, the best-scorers of Round 1 will proceed to Round 2'; Rocket City Math League has levels 'Explorer (Pre-Algebra) to Discovery (Comprehensive)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizing authority / host institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Many entries specify the organization or institution that runs or hosts the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Australian Mathematics Competition, run by the Australian Maths Trust'; 'The Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC) based out of the University of Waterloo hosts long-standing national competitions for grade levels 7–12.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic or linguistic orientation vs open participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contests are targeted at particular regions or language groups but may allow broader participation (e.g., mainly for French-speaking countries but not limited by language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Championnat International de Jeux Mathématiques et Logiques — for all ages, mainly for French-speaking countries, but participation is not limited by language.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize / recognition scope (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.description: While not always explicit, many competitions imply awards, selection, or recognition at local/national/international levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include competitions that serve as 'selection events' for national teams or those described as 'premier national mathematics competition' suggesting prestige and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target participant grouping / representation (gender/region)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contests target specific participant groups (e.g., girls, regional teams) or require representation by region/country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'China Girls Mathematical Olympiad (CGMO) — held annually for teams of girls representing different regions within China and a few other countries.'
